record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Nonconstant steady states for nonlocal multispecies model
record.original_question: For the same nonlocal multispecies system ∂_t u_i = d_iΔu_i − ∇·(u_i∇(Σ_j=1^n γ_ij u_j g,R)), spatially constant steady states are obvious. Under zero-flux, homogeneous Neumann, or periodic boundary conditions, in what setting do spatially non-constant steady states exist on a bounded domain?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2. It is clear that spatially constant steady state solutions exist solving problem (2.10). In what context do spatially non-constant steady state solutions exist solving problem (2.10) when subject to zero-flux, homogeneous Neumann, or periodic boundary conditions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary. Consider $n\geq 2$ species with population densities $u_i(x,t)\geq 0$, $i=1,\dots,n$, satisfying the nonlocal advection–diffusion system
$$\partial_t u_i \;=\; d_i\,\Delta u_i \;-\; \nabla\!\cdot\!\Big(u_i\,\nabla\Big(\sum_{j=1}^n \gamma_{ij}\,(u_j * g_R)\Big)\Big), \qquad x\in\Omega,\;t>0,$$
where $d_i>0$ are diffusion coefficients, $\gamma_{ij}\in\mathbb{R}$ are inter- and intra-species interaction coefficients (positive for attraction, negative for repulsion), and the nonlocal perception is given by the convolution
$$(u_j * g_R)(x,t)\;=\;\int_\Omega g_R(x-y)\,u_j(y,t)\,dy,$$
with $g_R$ a fixed radially symmetric, nonnegative, integrable detection kernel of perception radius $R>0$. Impose one of: zero-flux boundary conditions, homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, or periodic boundary conditions (in the latter case $\Omega$ is taken to be a flat torus and the convolution defined accordingly).

Spatially constant equilibria $u_i(x)\equiv \bar u_i$ trivially satisfy the stationary problem. Determine necessary and/or sufficient conditions on the parameters $(d_i)$, the interaction matrix $(\gamma_{ij})$, the kernel $g_R$, the domain $\Omega$, and the prescribed total masses $\int_\Omega u_i\,dx$ under which there exist spatially non-constant classical (or weak) steady-state solutions of the system.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was posed as an open question in a 2022 survey on PDE models for cognitive animal movement. Subsequent work on the same multispecies nonlocal advection–diffusion system has addressed local/global existence (Giunta et al., SIADS 2022) and characterization of local-minimum-energy states under symmetric interactions, but a general existence theory for spatially non-constant steady states under zero-flux/Neumann/periodic conditions has not been established. The problem appears still open in general.

status_evidence.title: Local and Global Existence for Nonlocal Multispecies Advection-Diffusion Models
status_evidence.snippet: Existence theorems for nonlocal multispecies advection-diffusion models with arbitrary number of species; global in 1D, local in higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Existence theory developed but focused on time-dependent solutions, not classification of non-constant steady states.

status_evidence.title: Detecting minimum energy states and multi-stability in nonlocal advection–diffusion models for interacting species
status_evidence.snippet: Methods for determining qualitative structure of local minimum energy states under symmetric interactions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress for symmetric interaction matrices via energy minimization, leaving the general non-symmetric case open.
